Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

have one’s hands full phrase

also have my hands full, be swamped, be very busy, have enough to do, have one’s work cut out

classical

Cato in Charis.: jam apud vallum nostrī satis agēbant (Lewis & Short), s.v. satis
Plaut. Bacch. 4.3.23: nunc agitās sat tūte tuārum rērum (Lewis & Short)
Traupman p. 99: satagere

satis agere (satagere)

satis (sat) with agō, often written as one word

have enough to do, have one’s hands full

Lewis & Short s.v. satis: “to have enough to do, have one’s hands full; to be in trouble”. The thing that keeps one busy is in the genitive in comedy: sat agere suārum rērum.

SourcesLewis & Short: satis · Lewis & Short: satago
